what: Bottlenecks from about one fully tested alloy a day to ten (bottleneck.py): each machine's capacity per unit, and a ladder of scenarios on timelapse.py's schedule, generalised. A model, not a measurement.
question: Sterling, PR #318, 2026-11-08: 'Approx. one full alloy tested per day was the estimation. How can we get that up to 10/day? What would be required?'

attended.source: assumed: the share of each step the arm spends at the station, from the chapters

present_h.source: assumed: a tray presented for a load or an unload holds its Shuttle's opening 3 min beyond the arm's attended time (Kardex's tray change plus the arm's pick or place); Kardex's own access time is a question for Kardex

wash_h.source: notes/alloy_print.md: 12-15 min a sieve, about 75-90 min for the six

u_max.source: assumed: the share of its available hours a station can be booked before queues grow without bound in a schedule with this much variety

availability.value: out/upkeep_model.json availability (seed 303, at about one alloy a day)
availability.source: upkeep.py; at ten a day the usage-driven faults come ten times as often, so these are optimistic

shifts.source: assumed shift patterns for the crucible's person

ded.source: assumed: an MX-Lab plate of 8 small blocks, one composition each, blended in the melt pool from its six feeders; 8 h a plate with set-up, deposition, cooling and unloading

shift.source: assumed: one person on a day shift, for the atomizer's crucible (notes/crucible_automation.md)

run_starts.source: assumed: a run needs its person for the first 1.0 h (crucible out, cleaned, BN-coated or swapped, loaded), so three runs fit an 8 h shift

runs_per_day_ramp.source: assumed: two weeks of one run a day while the lab is commissioned, two of two

friday_pm.value: no run starts after 12:00 on Fridays

atomize_h.source: a run about 1 h with prep (AMAZEMET training T5, 21:50) and a full cool-down about 30 min (T3, 49:52), both in notes/crucible_automation.md; the person's hour is assumed

charge_per_run.source: four cups as long as the Oct 27 rod pieces, about 300 g (notes/alloy_atomize.md, 'Four cups a run'); chapter 1's 2.5 in cups hold 157 g

usable_frac.source: the Oct 27 bronze run: 91 % under 250 um (DAL #219, notes/alloy_atomize.md)

fines_frac.source: the same run: 17 % of the charge under 63 um, the MIDI's cut (DAL #219); an upper estimate for Al, which atomizes coarser

run_fail_every.source: assumed: one run in ten drips instead of atomizing, as the Oct 8 Al 6063 run did (notes/alloy_atomize.md)

screen_build_g.source: the MIDI's 55 mm reduction kit takes about 30 g (DAL #138, notes/alloy_print.md)

full_build_g.source: the full 170 mm cylinder, the lab's planning figure (powder-doser design/brainstorming.md section 3, notes/alloy_atomize.md)

build_fail_every.source: assumed: one screening build in seven cracks or delaminates, and that alloy stops at its powder data

promote_every.source: assumed: one fully tested alloy in ten is promoted to a full-plate build of chapter 5's E8 subsize bars

transfer_h.source: assumed: a unit's drive plus pick and place, about 6 min (the MiR250 at 0.3 m/s^2, props.ramp_secs; the arm's moves in chapters 1-7)

stream_mbps.source: assumed: each stream camera archived at 1 Mbit/s, 24 h a day
